title: Forces
introductionText:
Physics
Forces — Pushes and Pulls
The Big Idea: Nothing moves by itself. Everything that moves has been pushed or pulled. A push sends something away from you. A pull
brings it towards you.
Say It Like This
Read aloud, standing at a door
"When you push, you send the thing away from you. When you pull, you bring it towards you. Now — this door. Is it a push or a pull? What
about the drawer? What about the doorbell? What about a swing — ah, a swing is both!"
PUSH — away from me PULL — towards me
Also in this unit — the movement words
roll (a ball) • fly (a bird) • swim (a fish) • run (a child) • hop (a kangaroo) • slither (a snake) • crawl (a baby)
roll fly swim hop slither crawl
a ball a bird a fish a kangaroo a snake a baby
Act each one out together across the room — he will remember the words far better.
Try It at Home
Activity 1 — Float or sink
Fill a bowl or the sink. Line up: an apple, a stone, a closed plastic bottle, a metal spoon, a coin, a cork, a plastic pot, a small ball. He predicts
every single one first and you write the guesses in two columns. Then drop them in one at a time and check.
A lovely question to leave hanging: "A small metal nail sinks — so how does a huge metal ship float?" You do not have to answer it.
Wondering is the point.
Activity 2 — Make a sailboat
Fold a small boat from aluminium foil. Push a straw through a paper square to make a sail and stand it in the boat. Float it in the bowl and
blow. Then ask: "Did I push it or pull it?" (A push — with air.)
these FLOAT on top
apple bottle cork
stone coin spoon
these SINK to the bottom
Draw this tank on paper and let him place each object himself before you test it.
More examples to talk about
Pushes and pulls hiding all around the house: pressing a light switch (push), opening the fridge (pull), closing a zip (pull), kicking a ball
(push), brushing teeth (push and pull), stirring tea (push), a donkey cart in the street (pull), a swing (both).
A bigger push does more: roll a ball gently, then hard. Same ball, different push, different distance. Ask: "What did I change?"
Float and sink surprises to try: an orange floats with its peel on but sinks when you peel it. A grape sinks in plain water. A ball of foil sinks,
but the same foil shaped into a boat floats.
Key Words
force push pull float sink predict

sourceQuestions.sourceText:
Complete the sentences. Use: push, pull
a) When you , you move the object away from you.
b) When you , you move the object towards you.

Push, pull, or both? Write your answer next to each one:
a) a doorbell b) a drawer
c) a swing d) a shopping trolley
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: a) push b) pull c) both push and pull d) both push and pull

sourceQuestions.sourceText:
Write F for float or S for sink:
a) balloon b) stone c) metal nail d) cork
e) plastic pot f) glass marble
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: a) F b) S c) S d) F e) F f) S

sourceQuestions.sourceText:
Match the animal to the way it moves:
snake bird fish kangaroo baby
fly hop slither crawl swim
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: snake – slither | bird – fly | fish – swim | kangaroo – hop | baby – crawl

sourceQuestions.sourceText: You blow on a paper sailboat and it moves. Is that a push or a pull? PUSH / PULL
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: PUSH — the moving air pushes the sail.

sourceQuestions.sourceText: Name one thing in your house you have to pull to open, and one thing you have to push to make it work.
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: Pull: a drawer, a door handle, a zip, a curtain. Push: a doorbell, a light switch, a button, a trolley.

sourceQuestions.sourceText: Write two pushes and two pulls you have done today.
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText:
Child's own answers. Pushes: pressing a switch, kicking a ball, closing a door, pushing a trolley. Pulls: opening a drawer, pulling a zip, pulling
on socks, opening the fridge.

sourceQuestions.sourceText:
An orange floats when its peel is on. What do you think happens when you take the peel off?
I predict:
Now test it. What really happened?
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: It sinks. The peel is full of tiny air pockets that hold the orange up; take the peel off and there is nothing to keep it floating.

sourceQuestions.sourceText: When you push something, it moves ( towards you ) ( away from you )
Which one sinks? ( a cork ) ( a metal coin ) ( a closed plastic bottle )
A snake moves by ( hopping ) ( slithering ) ( flying )
To send a ball further you need a ( bigger push ) ( smaller push )
